parsed.basis: Upper Nile, centred on Malakal near the Sudan border, inherits South Sudan's national regime under which section 379 criminalises a male person dressing as a woman, punishable by up to three months' imprisonment, exposing a trans visitor presenting female in public without any sexual conduct being required. Consensual same-sex conduct carries up to ten years under a provision reported unenforced in State Department reporting from 2018 to 2022, while security forces were reported during that period to harass, arrest, detain, beat and torture LGBTQI+ persons. There is no hate-crime or anti-discrimination protection, no known LGBTQ-support organisations, and a community rights group was raided in 2017, its staff detained, and the organisation intimidated into closing. Upper Nile has experienced prolonged conflict, displacement and fragmented security and judicial presence, with limited medical services and no documented local protective exception to the national regime.
